summary: The main hypothesis was confirmed: a simulated annealing approach with nearest-neighbor-guided 2-opt and efficient penalty delta computation scored 78.88 out of 100, a 2.35× improvement over the baseline probe score of 33.5. The key enabler was an O(segment/10) penalty recomputation that allowed evaluating large 2-opt segments (up to 5000 cities) within the 2-second time limit.
key_points: Score achieved: 78.88/100, up from 33.46 baseline — a substantial improvement confirming the algorithmic strategy works well.

The efficient delta computation (only checking every 10th step for penalty changes during segment reversal) was the critical optimization, reducing per-move cost from O(N) to O(segment/10) and enabling much larger neighborhood exploration.
Nearest-neighbor-guided 2-opt focused search on city pairs that are geographically close but far apart in tour order — exactly the highest-value improvements — rather than random pair selection.

Roughly 21 points of headroom remain (78.88 vs 100); further gains could come from 3-opt/LK moves, better prime-city scheduling at penalty positions (every 10th step), or longer SA cooling schedules tuned to stay within the time budget.
